newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Imperial sees Rizla boost abroad.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Imperial sees Rizla boost abroad.

text.p: Imperial Tobacco Group Plc said on Tuesday that it expected its 185 million stg investment in the handrolled tobacco paper group Rizla International BV to greatly enhance its expansion internationally.
"Imperial Tobacco is a relatively late entrant to international markets but is making some very fast strides in growth," chief executive Gareth Davis said in an interview.
"International profits rose 55 percent last year and Rizla have a large market share in seven or eight European countries, so obviously there are significant opportunities."

He added: "We use the same retailers and outlets in a number countries, especially the UK, but Rizla is active in over 70 countries and we overlap in about 20. Obviously we are looking to extract the potential we see at Rizla for increased profitability and productivity."
Davis said Imperial Tobacco, which was demerged from Hanson Plc in October, had been able to take advantage of its new-found freedom.
"It is a company we have been interested in for many years," he said, but added that demerger had preoccupied Imperial Tobaco last year.
Davis said the Rizla acquisition was "very much in line with our strategy at demerger of focusing on tobacco and tobacco-related products".
But he said this was not the start of "a great acquisition trail" for Imperial. "It was very much an acquisition opportunity."

The purchase price of 168 million stg in cash plus 17 milion stg of Rizla debt will be financed from Imperial's banking facilities. Davis said the purchase would have "a non-material effect on interest cover", which would be reduced to around 4.0 from 4.3.
Davis also told Reuters he did not see any job losses among Rizla's 714 employees as a result of the acquisition.
"We do see scope for productivity improvements but the plants are working at capacity," Davis said.

Imperial Tobacco said the company, based in Breda in the Netherlands, would continue to be run as a separate division, with the existing management remaining in place. Rizla has production facilities in Belgium, Wales and southern France.
Rizla, which was founded in 1796, is the world's largest producer and seller of handrolling tobacco papers, with around 66 percent of the world market share in branded products.
In 1996 it posted a trading profit of 23 million stg on sales of 74 million stg, and had net tangible assets of around 17 million stg.
Shares in Imperial were up 4 1/2 pence to 389 in early trading.
